sources.entry: OliveTin - Web interface for running Linux shell commands. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Go

summary.one_liner: OliveTin is a web interface that gives safe, simple access to predefined Linux shell commands, written in Go.
summary.what_it_does: OliveTin turns predefined shell commands into touch-friendly buttons in a web UI so people can run them without a terminal. Actions can prompt for typed and validated arguments, including defaults and dropdowns, before running. Command output is shown live along with success status and duration. Every action run is logged with who ran it, when, and whether it succeeded. Dashboards can group actions by managed entities such as servers or containers. Configuration is done in YAML, and the web UI is a single page app using a REST/Connect RPC API.
use_cases: give family members a button to restart a service
let junior admins run scripts through a form with dropdowns
trigger wake-on-lan or other commands from wall-mounted tablets
run long shell commands like system updates from a phone
grant temporary SSH access by running a timed firewall command
how_to_run: Read the installation guide at docs.olivetin.app
Install as a Linux package, Linux container, or on FreeBSD, Windows, or macOS (per the docs)
notable: Predefined commands only: users run what the admin configured, not arbitrary shell input
Argument forms with typed, validated fields, defaults, and dropdowns
Per-action execution logs showing who ran what and the outcome
No telemetry, no user tracking, and no internet connection required for core functions
Single edition with all features; no paid core/pro/enterprise tiers
caveats: Donations and sponsorship are not accepted, per the README
Installation and usage details live in external docs rather than the README
keywords: run scripts from a web page
safe shell access for non-technical users
alternative to ssh for family members
